column1: # Game profile of OCTOPATH TRAVELER (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.0.5 = v327680).
# Square Enix / Acquire, Unreal Engine 4.18 (project Kingship), SDK 3.5.1, NVN; subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie. Two legacy version 4 paks with zlib blocks, the shaders inline in the cooked packages
# (shader_split.py ue_legacy_jobs, decoded by uepak.py without the game). Started from the survey's provisional profile with the values of seedds/nxnative's Mac bring-up of this game;
# brought up on Android (Red Magic Astra) on 2026-11-03
# menus and the battle commands take the D-pad
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so there is no virtual address memory: nninitStartup sets a heap of pool − used (3.08 GB) and Unreal runs on it, with no engine address region.
# The 4 GB block of the games without virtual address memory: 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + the heap region
# each streamed texture has a virtual pool of its own (0x20000 to 0x560000 bytes) that it maps in parts: sparse, read through the page table (hle_nvn.c vpool_reserve)
# the rewritten modules (about 120 MB) are more than the default 64 MB of used memory the game takes off the pool for its heap
# Unreal writes some textures from the CPU into CPU-uncached pools after creating them and never flushes them (its UI images, the world map, the sprite sheets)
